OPERATOR INSIGHT · COMBINES PRICING + COST OF ELECTRICITY

Retail energy $0.45/kWh − electricity cost $0.16/kWh = $0.29/kWh energy spread

Spread before payment fees, demand charges, networking, and maintenance. It is not profit — it is the margin available to cover everything else. The current admin keeps retail price and electricity cost on separate screens; Bizwerx OS puts the spread on one card.

Chargers

14 connectors across the 4 Fresno sites, each with its own meter register. The 1600 Fulton DC cabinet counts once, with two connectors: DC-001 and Charger 1. Start or stop a connector and watch Sessions and the OCPP Log respond.

Sessions & Payments

Sessions move Created → Hold Placed → Start Requested → Charging → Settling → Settled. Money moves only in Settling, billed from the meter register (meterStop − meterStart). Select a session to inspect its payment math.

Payment ledger

Every hold, capture, release, dedupe, and alert — the money audit trail

    OCPP Log

    Live OCPP 1.6J exchange, simplified payloads. CSMS → CP is the OS; CP → CSMS is the charger.

    Test Lab

    Scripted failure drills against the live engine. Run one, then check Sessions, the OCPP Log, and the ledger to see how it was handled.

    A

    Charger drops offline mid-session, then replays its stop — twice

    Sinexcel DC 301 is charging now. This drill cuts its connection, lets the session finish on the charger itself, then reconnects — and the charger replays its queued StopTransaction two times, the way real firmware does after an outage.

    What it provesThe ledger deduplicates on transaction ID + meterStop. The replay is logged, acknowledged, and ignored — the driver is charged exactly once.

    Ready. Session on DC 301 is live.

    B

    Driver pays, never plugs in

    A driver starts a session on AC Pro 012 from their phone, the $30 hold is placed, the OS requests a start — and no car ever connects. The 90-second plug-in window (compressed here to a few seconds) runs out.

    What it provesA hold is not a charge. On timeout the session fails cleanly and the full $30 hold is released — $0 captured, nothing to refund because nothing was taken.

    Ready. AC Pro 012 is available.

    C

    A session with no stop message — the orphan

    A session starts on Supernova 202, delivers energy, and then goes silent: no StopTransaction, no heartbeat, charger unreachable. Left alone, that is an open hold and an unbillable session.

    What it provesThe orphan sweeper finds sessions with no stop and stale meter data, settles them from the last MeterValues reading, releases the rest of the hold, and alerts the operator.

    Ready. Supernova 202 is available.

    D

    SIM payment lapses — charger healthy, reported down

    Chargers connect by Wi-Fi or SIM. AC Pro 009 runs on SIM. When the SIM data plan lapses, the charger cannot reach the OS or its separate POS terminal, so drivers see it as down — while the charger itself is completely healthy. This is a communications problem, not a hardware failure.

    What it provesThe operator view separates “No connection” from “Faulted,” shows the comms path (Wi-Fi or SIM) on every charger, and phrases the alert with a likely cause — renew the SIM plan — instead of dispatching a repair crew for a healthy charger.

    Ready. AC Pro 009 is available on SIM.

      Installed hardware

      Your units at Fulton Street, photographed on site. The Autel MaxiCharger AC Pro speaks OCPP 1.6J and 2.0.1 with third-party cloud support in Autel's own spec.

      Certification queue

      Any OCPP charger can join the network. A model is listed as tested only after it passes a certification pass: simulator first, then a lab unit.
